articles.title: Watch Travis Kelce Pass Rob Gronkowski on Historic NFL Milestone List in Chiefs vs. Cardinals Video
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce picked up an 8-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals, but it was more than just a usual touchdown.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce picked up an 8-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals, but it was more than just a usual touchdown.

With the catch, Kelce passed former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers star tight end Rob Gronkowski for third place for the most total touchdowns by a tight end in league history with 109, including postseason play. Kelce now only trails Pro Football Hall of Famers Antonio Gates (118) and Tony Gonzalez (115).

Sunday was also Kelce's 100th career regular season game at Arrowhead Stadium, the fourth Chiefs player to ever reach that number. He and Mahomes passed Gates and Philip Rivers earlier this season for most yards (9,365) by a quarterback and tight end duo in NFL history.

So it's just another day, another milestone for Kelce, who notched his 110th career touchdown later in the game with a 22-yard TD in the second quarter on Sunday.

Per ESPN's Nate Taylor , Kelce became the fourth player ever (Jim Thorpe, Steve Young and Jerry Rice) two score two touchdowns in one half at age 37 or older.

"That's good company right there," Kelce said, per Taylor. "That's an iconic group."

articles.title: Dak Prescott Shines in Cowboys' Win vs. Titans, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Lamb, Cam Ward, More
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys put up a 50-burger on the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys put up a 50-burger on the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon.

Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and Co. did whatever they wanted against one of the worst defenses in the NFL on the way to a 51-30 victory.

Six different players scored a touchdown in the rout, which was headlined by Dak Prescott's 300-yard passing day and 100-yard receiving performances by Lamb and George Pickens.

Dallas went a perfect six-for-six on its opening six drives.

Lamb and Pickens each caught a touchdown pass in the second quarter as part of the offensive onslaught.

The pair of passing touchdowns followed two first-quarter rushing touchdowns from Javonte Williams and KaVontae Turpin.

Williams was the only Cowboys player to find the end zone on two occasions in the rout.

Prescott led the Cowboys on four scoring drives in each half. The only drive that didn't result in a touchdown ended in a Brandon Aubrey field goal in the fourth quarter.

Prescott is on a three-game streak of 300-yard passing performances. That bodes well for the Dallas offense as it tries to make a run at the New York Giants at the top of the NFC East.

Lamb and Pickens combined for 234 receiving yards. Lamb is up to five 100-yard receiving games in 2026, while Pickens has three, including two in the last two weeks.

The Titans scored over 20 points for the fifth consecutive game, but they were never able to keep pace with the Cowboys.

Cam Ward threw for 248 yards, while Tony Pollard eclipsed the 100-yard rushing mark against his former team.

The Cowboys will continue their push toward the NFC East title on Thanksgiving Day at home against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Titans are back in action on Sunday against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: Eagles Beat Steelers to Extend Historic Streak, Box Score Stats for Rodgers, Saquon, Top Players
articles.summary: The seven-game losing streak is over.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) managed to beat the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, 19-16, led by Saquon Barkley's nice day on the ground and a stout defensive effort. The Steelers have now lost 12 straight games in Philadelphia dating back to the 1965 season.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

The Eagles came out pretty hot in this game, jumping out to a 13-0 lead, highlighted by a 38-yard touchdown run by Saquon Barkley and a strong defensive showing.

Their upset bid was aided by DK Metcalf, who was ejected in the third quarter.

And yet the second half threatened to follow a familiar script for the Birds.

For much of the 2026 season, the team's offense has been awful in the second half, failing to stay on the field or put points on the board. That puts pressure on an otherwise solid defense, and eventually the dam breaks.

Part of that was true on Sunday. The offense had a fumble, two three-and-outs, four punts and only managed two field goals in the second half against the Steelers. But this time the defense was able to hold out, which perhaps could be partially credited to a pretty miserable offensive effort from Pittsburgh.

The Steelers at least put up a late fight. But too little and too late.

If you like offense, this wasn't the game for you. The Eagles had 213 yards of total offense. The Steelers had 255. There were two touchdowns and seven field goals. There were no fireworks in this one; there weren't even sparklers or flickering candles.

Either way, Philly's losing streak is over, while the Steelers have now lost two straight. Suddenly, there are very real questions about whether this Pittsburgh team has the juice to make a postseason appearance.

Sunday wasn't a great sign in that regard.

articles.title: Bucs RB Bucky Irving celebrates touchdown by smacking Vita Vea's stomach like a bass drum
articles.summary: You've heard of the 'Sexy Dexy.' Get ready for the 'belly celly.'
articles.body:
Some NFL players know how to start a conversation with their touchdown celebrations. On Sunday, Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving joined up with nose tackle Vita Vea to add to that list.

In the third quarter of Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions, Irving pushed through the defense from the 1-yard line for a touchdown . That score pulled Tampa Bay within three points of Detroit's 17-14 lead, and gave the Buccaneers momentum.

Therefore, it was only fair to celebrate in wild fashion. After the touchdown was called, Irving called over Vea, who lifted his shirt to reveal his bare stomach. Irving then smacked Vea's tummy three times.

It's not entirely clear what Irving and Vea had in mind, though the "belly celly" seemingly imitated the large bass drums sometimes pounded by other pro and college football teams.

The celebrations didn't stop coming in the second half of Sunday's game: In addition to Irving's rushing touchdown, which came right after a score from Lions receiver Jameson Williams, Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs scored two touchdowns to grow the team's lead. Baker Mayfield found Ted Hurst III with seconds remaining, but Tampa Bay's onside kick failed, allowing Detroit to take a 31-21 win .

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza Updates LinkedIn After Raiders Trade Kirk Cousins, Reflects on 1st NFL Start
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback did what many people do after their first day on the job: post on LinkedIn.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback did what many people do after their first day on the job: post on LinkedIn.

It just so happened his first day got a little more attention.

Mendoza, the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, took to his LinkedIn page on Sunday, a week after making his first NFL start against the Seattle Seahawks last week.

"A lot to learn from my first NFL start," Mendoza wrote on LinkedIn. "Grateful for my family, friends, and Raider Nation for the support! Looking forward to getting better and earning the trust of my teammates and coaches every day."

Mendoza officially became the Raiders' starting QB after they traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota earlier in November.

LinkedIn has long been Mendoza's social media of choice, as opposed to more popular options for athletes such as Instagram and X. The 23-year-old's only social media presence is on the job-networking website, where he has posted career updates since his days playing collegiately at California.

articles.title: Caleb Williams' Bears Outlast Saints, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Shough, Swift, Top Players
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears and Caleb Williams came away with a 21-13 victory over Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints at home on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears and Caleb Williams came away with a 21-13 victory over Tyler Shough and the New Orleans Saints at home on Sunday.

The Bears entered the matchup as 11.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and came away with an eight-point victory despite a relatively quiet performance from Williams, who finished with 181 passing yards, two touchdowns and an interception.

Williams recorded his second-lowest passing yardage total of the season, with his lowest coming in Week 2 when the Bears fell to the Minnesota Vikings 9-3 behind 138 yards from Williams.

Chicago's win extended its winning streak to five games, improving its record to 8-2 and keeping the Bears atop the tightly contested NFC North race ahead of an important divisional matchup against the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving.

The Saints' loss dropped them to 3-7, leaving them tied with the Atlanta Falcons near the bottom of the NFC South as the two teams face very different divisional outlooks.

It was a messy game for the Saints, who scored 10 points in the first half before being held to a field goal in the second.

Despite a disastrous second quarter that included two turnovers and a missed field goal, Shough found Alvin Kamara for a short touchdown before the Saints closed out the half with a field goal.

Meanwhile, Chicago opened the game with a field goal before Williams connected with D'Andre Swift and tight end Colston Loveland for touchdown passes in the second quarter. Williams threw an interception before halftime, but the Bears held onto a 16-10 lead.

It was a quiet second half for both teams. The Bears added a field goal in the third quarter before a safety tacked on two more points after Shough was sacked in the end zone.

Chicago committed its second turnover of the game in the fourth quarter, while the Saints notched their first score since the 54-second mark of the second quarter as the Bears secured the home win.

Chicago faces the Lions on the road in a decisive Thanksgiving matchup at 1 p.m. ET, while the Saints travel to face the Cincinnati Bengals next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 'Unacceptable,' Steelers' Mike McCarthy Calls Out DK Metcalf After WR Ejected in Loss vs. Eagles
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers had to play a large portion of Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles without a key receiver after DK Metcalf was ejected in the second half after receiving two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers had to play a large portion of Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles without a key receiver after DK Metcalf was ejected in the second half after receiving two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties.

After the game, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy called Metcalf's actions "unacceptable."

Metcalf's ejection came after he was seen on video putting his hand inside the face mask of Eagles' Cooper DeJean, who then seemed to be complaining about being poked in the eye.

Metcalf hadn't been a major contributor on offense before being ejected, as he had just one catch for two yards on four targets. The Steelers lost the game 19-16, marking the Eagles' third win of the season and their first since Week 2. They had lost seven consecutive games coming into the matchup.

Unfortunately for the Steelers, Sunday's incident wasn't the first time Metcalf has let his anger get the best of him.

It was the third time since he was drafted in 2019 that Metcalf has been disqualified from a game, matching him with San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw for the most during that time period.

Last season, Metcalf was suspended for two games after an altercation with a Detroit Lions fan.

Whether Metcalf will face a further suspension remains to be seen.

The 28-year-old Metcalf has had a bit of a down year by his standards, recording just 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns in 10 games. He's eclipsed the 100-yard mark just one time so far.

Perhaps Sunday's ejection was the culmination of his frustration with this year's struggles.

articles.title: Travis Kelce scores twice, passes Rob Gronkowski on all-time tight end touchdown list in blowout win over Cardinals
articles.summary: Travis Kelce scored two touchdowns in the Chiefs' dominant win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
articles.body:
Travis Kelce finally jumped Rob Gronkowski on Sunday afternoon.

Kelce hauled in an 8-yard touchdown early in the Kansas City Chiefs' 34-7 blowout win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday . That marked the 109th score of Kelce's career, which moved him to third on the NFL's all-time touchdown list by a tight end and broke a tie with Gronkowski. The longtime New England Patriots star finished his career with 108 touchdowns.

Now, only Hall of Famers Antonio Gates, with 118, and Tony Gonzalez, with 115, sit ahead of Kelce.

Kelce scored again in the second quarter when Patrick Mahomes found him for a 22-yard touchdown. Kelce jumped up and made the grab between a trio of Cardinals.

That touchdown put the Chiefs up 23-7 at the time.

Kelce finished the game with 74 receiving yards on six receptions in the 27-point win, which pushed the Chiefs to 8-2 on the season. Mahomes went 27-of-39 passing for 324 yards with three touchdowns. He sat early in the fourth quarter with the win all but secured. The Cardinals (3-8) have lost three straight.

Sunday was also Kelce's 100th regular-season game at Arrowhead Stadium, which made him the fourth player in team history to reach that mark. Kelce has already broken the NFL record for most yards after catch in league history this season, too, and earlier this fall Mahomes and Kelce surpassed Gates and Philip Rivers for the most yards generated by a tight end and quarterback duo in NFL history.

Kelce has spent his entire career with the Chiefs, who first selected him out of Cincinnati in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft. He has 13,588 receiving yards in his career, which trails only Gonzalez among tight ends, and he has 586 receiving yards and four touchdowns this season.

While Kelce's career is winding down, he is only nine touchdowns shy of becoming the all-time tight end touchdown leader. That may be tough to pull off with just seven games left in the regular season, but the mark is in reach.

articles.title: Jerry Jones Says Cowboys Win 'Gives Me Hope' After Scoring 51 vs. Titans Amid NFL Playoff Race
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys scored touchdowns in their first six possessions of their 51-30 blowout win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, and owner Jerry Jones was thrilled about it.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys scored touchdowns in their first six possessions of their 51-30 blowout win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, and owner Jerry Jones was thrilled about it.

The Cowboys (5-6) stayed in striking distance of the New York Giants (5-3-1) for first place in the NFC East and are a game and a half behind Green Bay for a wild-card spot with a dominant offensive showing. Dallas scored in its first eight offensive series overall on Sunday.

"It gives me hope that we can do some of the things that we want to do," Jones told reporters, according to DallasCowboys.com reporter Tommy Yarrish. "We want to get better defensively, and we want to execute like that offensively. That thing went exactly like it was mapped out to go. Have a balanced running game with that passing game, and we used our top players to make things happen out there. I really thought we pressured them up real good… Really proud."

Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns while rushing for another against the hapless Titans defense. Tennessee is now 1-9 and in line for the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both caught TD passes as well during the onslaught.

articles.title: DK Metcalf ejected after another dustup with Eagles' Cooper DeJean, unsportsmanlike conduct penalty amid Steelers loss
articles.summary: Metcalf recorded only 1 reception for 2 yards in Philadelphia before his disqualification late in the third quarter.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf had more costly penalties on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field than receptions.

Metcalf was ejected with only one reception to his name after the second of those infractions late in the third quarter during a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. The final straw was when he was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct.

He was called for taunting in the wake of his latest dustup with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean. And so Metcalf, who was notably suspended two games last season for swinging at a Detroit Lions fan during a sideline altercation , was disqualified, with Philly fans waving goodbye to him as he walked to the tunnel.

The taunting penalty occurred in the fallout of a third-and-8 incompletion from Aaron Rodgers with less than five minutes left in the third quarter. Rodgers was looking for wide receiver Germie Bernard toward the left pylon. Metcalf was lined up on the right side of the field pre-snap, in the slot, where he was matched up with DeJean.

Following the play, the CBS Sports broadcast showed Metcalf and Philadelphia safety Marcus Epps getting into it. Metcalf had to be restrained by Pittsburgh wide receiver Roman Wilson and tight end Pat Freiermuth.

After Metcalf walked off to the sideline, the broadcast displayed another clip that exhibited Metcalf putting his hand into DeJean's face mask. Metcalf "just missed" poking him in the eye, DeJean told reporters postgame.

"He wasn't getting the ball a whole lot during that game," DeJean said, via 97.5 The Fanatic . "Some receivers, they let that get to them. Obviously he tried to take it out on me."

Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said the referee told him that Metcalf "poked the defender in the eye."

Not only was Metcalf DQ'd, but he also lost his team 15 yards. That backed up a Chris Boswell field-goal attempt, which ended up being from 52 yards out. Fortunately for Pittsburgh, Boswell made the kick to cut the team's deficit to 16-9.

Even with some help from little-known wideout Max Hurleman in Metcalf's absence — the former undrafted free agent hauled in a late touchdown after being elevated from the practice squad — the Steelers (6-4) fell by three points.

In turn, the injury-ravaged Eagles (3-7) snapped their seven-game losing streak.

Afterward, McCarthy was asked about his confidence level in Metcalf.

"I think our men do a good job of looking in the mirror, and we got a short week," McCarthy said, alluding to Pittsburgh's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos coming up.

"But yeah, no, we'll sit down and address everything, especially, you know, we need him. We need him in those games, and that's not acceptable to be thrown out of a game. He's one of the 48 [active players]. It's about everything we do through the week is to put those guys in position to be successful."

Metcalf's first penalty arrived with just under 13 minutes to go in the third quarter. He was blocking DeJean on a 5-yard carry from Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren. That turned into extracurricular activity.

Metcalf and DeJean were tangled up after the play. They had to be separated, and Metcalf was assessed an unnecessary roughness penalty.

That infraction effectively erased a positive first-down gain by Warren, keeping the Steelers at the doorstep of their own end zone.

They ended up punting three plays later.

Metcalf clocked out with one catch for two receiving yards in the defeat. He came into the day with 35 receptions, 432 receiving yards and two touchdowns. In the past four games, he's reeled in a combined six passes.

In March 2025, the Steelers acquired Metcalf from the Seattle Seahawks in a trade. Pittsburgh gave up a 2025 second-round pick and signed the two-time Pro Bowl receiver to a five-year extension reportedly worth $150 million.

The Steelers went on to trade wideout George Pickens to the Dallas Cowboys later that offseason.

Metcalf, a 2019 second-round pick, has been ejected three times since entering the NFL and is tied with San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw for the most disqualifications in that span, according to ESPN . Infamously, Metcalf's aforementioned sideline altercation with a Lions fan last season didn't result in a penalty or an ejection, as it wasn't seen by officials in real time.

articles.title: Eagles' Cooper DeJean Explains DK Metcalf Ejection, Says Steelers WR 'Just Missed' Poking Him in Eye
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean confirmed that DK Metcalf "almost" poked him in the eyes and "just missed" during a second-half scuffle between the pair, leading to the Pittsburgh Steelers' wideout being ejected after receiving a second personal foul.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean confirmed that DK Metcalf "almost" poked him in the eyes and "just missed" during a second-half scuffle between the pair, leading to the Pittsburgh Steelers' wideout being ejected after receiving a second personal foul.

"We were just competing," DeJean told reporters. "Things like that happen in football. It wasn't anything crazy, no one was really saying anything, it was just two guys going at it. He was trying to block me, I was trying to get him off of me. Things like that and then it obviously carried over to whatever that was at the end when he got thrown out."

Mike McCarthy Calls Out DK After Ejection

Metcalf was flagged for unnecessary roughness on his first personal foul in the first half and was penalized for taunting on the second. He exited the game with one catch for two yards on four targets.

"This was definitely a game we expected to win. I think his particular case performance-wise, I think our process, I think our men do a good job of looking in the mirror. And you know, we've got a short week. We'll sit down and address everything," head coach Mike McCarthy told reporters after the game. "Especially, we need him. We need him in those games, and that's not acceptable to get thrown out of the game. He's one of the 48. It's about everything we do through the week is to put those guys in position to be successful."

It was the third ejection of Metcalf's career, tied for the most among active players with San Francisco 49ers' linebacker Dre Greenlaw. And it comes amid a particularly disappointing season, as Metcalf has registered just 36 catches for 434 yards and two touchdowns.

Whether a suspension will follow remains to be seen, though the incident will be reviewed by the league office. Metcalf was suspended two games last season in December after having a physical confrontation with a Detroit Lions fan.

articles.title: Broncos, ESPN, Fox Sports and others honor longtime linebacker, analyst Tom Jackson after his death
articles.summary: Plenty in the NFL media world honored Tom Jackson in their coverage on Sunday.
articles.body:
The NFL world honored longtime Denver Broncos linebacker and ESPN analyst Tom Jackson on Sunday , days after his death.

Jackson died Friday , friend and colleague Chris Berman announced Sunday during ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown." He was 75.

Jackson spent 14 seasons in the league with the Broncos from 1973-1986. He earned three Pro Bowl nods and appeared in two Super Bowls with the franchise. He retired with 191 games played in his career, which was the fourth-most in Broncos history. Jackson, who played at Louisville before landing in the NFL, was inducted into Denver's Ring of Fame in 1992.

The Broncos honored Jackson ahead of their win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, and played a video tribute to him on the scoreboard at Empower Field before kickoff.

Then after the contest, the Broncos gave the game ball to Jackson's family.

Lee Corso, who coached Jackson at Louisville, called him the "best football player I ever had."

"Not only that, he was the best leader I ever had," Corso said in a statement . "My condolences to Tom's family in this difficult time."

After his playing career ended, Jackson joined ESPN in 1987 and quickly became a fixture in the network's NFL coverage. He worked there for nearly three decades until he retired in 2016, and spent nearly the entire time working alongside Berman.

"All of us are stunned. We've lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet," Berman said. "I was fortunate, as you know, to work side-by-side with him for 30 years on 'NFL Primetime' and 'NFL Gameday,' now 'Sunday NFL Countdown.'" "Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst," he added. "There was nobody kinder, there was nobody more thoughtful, more loyal, more engaging than Tom Jackson."

"All of us are stunned. We've lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet," Berman said. "I was fortunate, as you know, to work side-by-side with him for 30 years on 'NFL Primetime' and 'NFL Gameday,' now 'Sunday NFL Countdown.'"

"Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst," he added. "There was nobody kinder, there was nobody more thoughtful, more loyal, more engaging than Tom Jackson."

Jackson was behind the iconic "Jacked Up!" segment each week during the NFL season, which showcased the hardest hits throughout the league. The segment was eventually phased out as concern for head trauma and serious injury grew throughout football.

ESPN brought that segment back Sunday, and ended it with a huge hit of Jackson's.

Fox Sports also honored Jackson during its coverage, and played the "NFL Primetime" music while showing halftime highlights Sunday.

"The NFL lost a wonderful man with the passing of Tom Jackson. Along with millions of fans, I will always remember him as a player and broadcaster, but also as a friend. He was an outstanding player whose toughness and leadership helped define an era of Broncos football. He brought credibility, passion and humor to everything he did, and generations of fans came to know him through his work at ESPN. Tom helped fans enjoy and better understand football, always bringing the perspective of someone who loved the game and the people who play it. More importantly, he earned the respect and friendship of players, coaches and everyone who had the privilege of knowing and working with him."

Rich Eisen, Keyshawn Johnson, Tedy Bruschi, Randy Moss, Adam Schefter, Bill Cower and plenty of others in the NFL media world all honored Jackson and spoke about him on their respective platforms.

Through charity visits in South Africa and Brazil, she used her love of soccer to connect with young people who saw the game as more than entertainment.Gracie Hunt took her passion for soccer to children in South Africa and BrazilGracie Hunt's charitable journey had started at a young age. In 2010, she joined Athletes in Action for a soccer clinic in South Africa, where she spent time with children from underprivileged communities. The experience gave her an opportunity to share the sport she loved with youngsters who did not always have access to organised athletic programmes.For Gracie, these visits were about more than teaching football skills. Sports could give children a place to belong, help them build friendships and teach lessons that stayed with them long after a game ended.Her efforts continued in 2014 when she travelled to Brazil during the World Cup period. Rather than limiting her involvement to the excitement surrounding the tournament, she helped bring soccer equipment to children living in the country's favelas.Access to basic sporting equipment could make a real difference in communities where families faced financial challenges. Her charitable work had developed alongside her love for athletics, not simply as an extension of her family's football legacy.Gracie Hunt wanted sports to create opportunities beyond the playing fieldHer experiences with disadvantaged children also connected with a wider belief in the value of sports. Gracie later developed Breaking Barriers Through Sports, an initiative designed to help young people access athletic opportunities and build confidence.Her own sporting journey had not been without setbacks. Multiple concussions forced her to step away from competitive soccer, changing the future she had once imagined for herself. Yet her connection with sports remained.Instead of allowing that disappointment to define her relationship with athletics, she found another way to stay involved. Helping children experience the benefits of sports gave her passion a different direction.Her work also reflected an important issue: talent alone did not guarantee every child an equal chance to participate. articles.summary: DK Metcalf was ejected from Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles in the third, leaving the Pittsburgh Steelers without one of their top receivers for the rest of the way.
articles.body:
DK Metcalf was ejected from Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles in the third, leaving the Pittsburgh Steelers without one of their top receivers for the rest of the way.

Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers called Metcalf's ejection "dissapointing."

"I don't know what was going on out there or what was happening, but we can't have two of those," Rodgers said (31-second mark).

Mike McCarthy Calls Out DK After Ejection

Rodgers was also coy regarding what his message to Metcalf was after the game.

"I'm not gonna tell you that," he said. "I talked to DK and we're all good friends."

Metcalf received his first unsportsmanlike conduct penalty in the first half after an altercation before receiving another in the second after getting into it with Eagles safety Marcus Epps after an incomplete pass from Rodgers to Germie Bernard.

After jawing with Epps, a scrum broke out around the two and Metcalf appeared to put his hand in the facemask of Cooper DeJean. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said after the game that an official told him that Metcalf poked an Eagles player in the eye.

"This was definitely a game we expected to win. I think his particular case performance-wise, I think our process, I think our men do a good job of looking in the mirror. And you know, we've got a short week," McCarthy told reporters after the game. "We'll sit down and address everything.

"Especially, we need him. We need him in those games, and that's not acceptable to get thrown out of the game. He's one of the 48. It's about everything we do through the week is to put those guys in position to be successful."

McCarthy added that an internal suspension is "definitely" on the table for Metcalf after his third career ejection.

Metcalf has had a dissapointing season with just 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns in 10 games, and an ejection on Sunday only adds to it.

articles.title: The boy who became the storm: How Stefon Diggs turned childhood loss and family struggles into an NFL career
articles.summary: Stefon Diggs has spent years proving himself on the biggest stage in American football, but his journey began with a loss that changed his life forever.
articles.body: Stefon Diggs has spent years proving himself on the biggest stage in American football, but his journey began with a loss that changed his life forever. At just 14, he lost his father, Aron Diggs, and suddenly had to take on responsibilities that most children never experience. From supporting his mother and younger siblings to fighting serious injuries and being overlooked in the NFL Draft, Diggs faced one challenge after another before becoming one of the league’s most respected wide receivers.Stefon Diggs’ childhood and his father’s death changed the way he saw lifeBorn on November 29, 1993, in Gaithersburg, Maryland, Stefon Marsean Diggs grew up in a family where football was more than just a sport. His father, Aron Diggs, played a major role in introducing him and his brothers to the game. He coached their youth football teams and made sure they understood the importance of discipline, hard work and staying focused on their goals.Aron was strict with his sons, but he wanted them to have the best possible future. Football became a regular part of their lives, and he spent hours helping them improve. Stefon was particularly close to his father, who had a big influence on the way he approached the game.However, the family faced a painful change in January 2008. Aron, who had been waiting for a heart transplant, died from congestive heart failure at the age of 39. Stefon was only 14 years old, while his younger brother Trevon was nine.Losing his father at such a young age was difficult for Stefon. He had lost the person who introduced him to football, guided him through life and encouraged him to dream big. His mother, Stephanie Diggs, also had to find a way to keep the family together while dealing with her own grief.She became the family’s main provider and worked long shifts as an Amtrak service attendant. She also took additional jobs at Target and Toys “R” Us to make sure her children had what they needed. It was not an easy situation, but she continued working hard for her family.Stefon understood that his younger siblings needed support, especially after losing their father. He began taking care of them and tried to become someone they could depend on. His younger brother Trevon would later speak about how much Stefon meant to him, describing his older brother as a father figure who was always there whenever he needed guidance.The responsibility was not something Stefon had planned for at 14, but he accepted it. His father had asked him to look after his mother, sister and brothers, and that message stayed with him.In a 2020 interview with GQ, Diggs spoke about how losing his father forced him to grow up quickly. He explained that he had to make decisions while thinking about his loved ones and younger siblings, rather than focusing only on himself.That experience also influenced his college decision. Despite receiving interest from several major football programmes, he chose the University of Maryland, partly because he wanted to stay close to home and remain involved in his younger brother’s life.His mother and siblings were an important part of every decision he made. Even when football started opening doors for him, he never wanted to move so far away that he could not be there for his family.From college injuries to NFL stardom: How Stefon Diggs proved his doubters wrongStefon Diggs attended Our Lady of Good Counsel High School in Olney, Maryland, where his football talent started attracting attention across the country. He became one of the most exciting young wide receivers in high school football and earned recognition as a five-star recruit.His performances made several major college programmes interested in signing him. However, Diggs eventually decided to stay close to home and joined the University of Maryland in 2012.He made an immediate impact during his freshman season, recording 54 catches for 848 receiving yards and six touchdowns. He also finished the year with 1,896 all-purpose yards, showing that he could contribute in several areas of the game.Things looked promising, but his college journey soon became difficult. During the 2013 season, Diggs suffered a broken right fibula against Wake Forest. The injury forced him to miss the final six games of the season, taking away an important opportunity to build on his early success.He returned in 2014, but another injury interrupted his progress. A lacerated kidney suffered during a game against Penn State became another major setback. For a young player hoping to reach the NFL, missing games and dealing with repeated injuries was far from ideal.Still, Diggs refused to give up on his dream. He finished his college career with 150 receptions, 2,227 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns in three seasons.The Minnesota Vikings selected him with the 146th overall pick in the fifth round of the 2015 NFL Draft. It was not the early selection many talented college players hope for, but Diggs finally had the opportunity he had worked towards since childhood.He made the most of it. Despite being inactive for Minnesota’s first three games, he finished his rookie season with 52 catches for 720 yards and four touchdowns. The Professional Football Writers Association also named him to its 2015 All-Rookie Team.His career continued to grow over the next few seasons. In 2017, he became part of one of the most memorable plays in NFL playoff history.During a divisional playoff game against the New Orleans Saints, quarterback Case Keenum threw a pass towards Diggs in the final seconds. Diggs caught the ball, avoided a tackle and ran into the end zone to give Minnesota a dramatic 29-24 victory. The play became known as the Minneapolis Miracle.It was a defining moment in his career, but Diggs was not finished. He recorded 102 catches for 1,021 yards in 2018 and followed that with 1,130 receiving yards in 2019. He had established himself as one of Minnesota’s leading offensive players.However, his time with the Vikings eventually came to an end. Diggs wanted a different opportunity and a bigger role in an offence that could make full use of his abilities. In March 2020, Minnesota traded him to the Buffalo Bills.The move changed the direction of his career.Playing alongside quarterback Josh Allen, Diggs became the main target in Buffalo’s passing game. During his first season with the Bills, he caught 127 passes for 1,535 yards and eight touchdowns. He led the NFL in both receptions and receiving yards, earned First-Team All-Pro honours and secured his first Pro Bowl selection.He continued to produce impressive numbers in Buffalo, recording 1,225 receiving yards in 2021, 1,429 in 2022 and 1,183 in 2023. His partnership with Allen helped the Bills become one of the strongest offensive teams in the league.After four successful seasons in Buffalo, Diggs was traded to the Houston Texans in April 2024. He started well, recording 47 catches for 496 yards and three touchdowns in eight games. However, a torn ACL ended his season early.The injury was another difficult moment for a player who had already spent years dealing with physical setbacks. Diggs had to work his way back once again, but he was not ready to walk away from football.In March 2025, he signed with the New England Patriots. He returned to the field and finished the season with 85 catches for 1,013 yards and four touchdowns. His performances helped New England reach Super Bowl LX against the Seattle Seahawks.Although the Patriots released him on March 11, 2026, another opportunity soon arrived. The Washington Commanders signed the veteran receiver on August 7, 2026, bringing him back to Maryland, the place where his football journey began.As of November 22, 2026, NFL.com lists Diggs with 36 catches for 386 yards and six touchdowns in eight appearances for Washington. At 32, he is still competing at the highest level and adding another chapter to a career that has taken him through several teams and difficult seasons.For Diggs, football has always been connected to something bigger than personal achievements. The boy who lost his father at 14 went on to build an NFL career while carrying the responsibility of supporting the people he loved. His journey has not been free of setbacks, but his ability to keep going has helped him earn his place among the league’s leading receivers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Temwa Chawinga and her teammates celebrated a title that had once seemed a distant goal for the young franchise.The victory carried significance beyond the final score. The Current had shown that investment in women's soccer could create a lasting sporting identity, attract major crowds and deliver success.For Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, the championship added another milestone to their connection with Kansas City. articles.title: Ravens silenced Marlon Humphrey for his words but what they'll hear after another loss will pale in comparison
articles.summary: Ravens tried to address criticism with Humphrey suspension but cannot quiet noise after 35-33 to the Carolina Panthers, their sixth consecutive loss.
articles.body: Days after silencing Marlon Humphrey for his disparaging words about their city, the Baltimore Ravens are going to wish they could silence a significant portion of their fans. Days after one of their coaches addressed the Humphrey issue, saying there is "freedom of speech but not freedom of consequences," the Ravens are staring at the consequences of being a bad football team. Days after basically not accepting Humphrey's apology for what he said on his podcast, the Ravens owe Baltimore an apology for their play on the field. RAVENS DIDN'T DISCIPLINE RECEIVER OVER DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ARREST BUT SUSPEND MARLON HUMPHREY OVER PODCAST COMMENTS Carolina Panthers 35. Baltimore Ravens 33. Welcome to the week that was and the season it has been for the Ravens. In a season that has been a bitter disappointment and now includes six consecutive losses, the Ravens spent two days last week addressing and re-addressing what seemed like an otherwise manageable controversy that Humphrey started. WOMAN KILLED NEAR RAVENS STADIUM SAME DAY MARLON HUMPHREY SENT HOME FOR JOKE ABOUT BALTIMORE CRIMINALITY Humphrey on his podcast was asked what it was Baltimore is best at making? "They're best at making criminals," he replied half-jokingly. The disparaging words lit a firestorm that became a national story last Wednesday and Thursday while the Ravens were trying to salvage this season. And it is unfortunate for everyone involved because ... NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE MESSAGING WHILE BATTLING DOMESTIC ABUSE, DRUNK DRIVING AND PROSTITUTION ARRESTS Let's handle that part first. Humphrey apologized immediately once this became a problem. And the Ravens seemed to accept that Wednesday as they prepared for Sunday's game against the Panthers. But seeing the negative media attention and backlash from fans and politicians and on social media, the Ravens took an extra step by suspending Humphrey on Thursday. The club in need of more talent, not less, sent one of its top four or five defensive backs home for the weekend and possibly longer. The team could have as easily decided to make it clear that it believed Humphrey was wrong, he apologized, and it was onward to Carolina. But the club instead bowed to outside opinions. All while making its secondary inside the team weaker. Baltimore allowed 35 points against Carolina. No, that doesn't imply Baltimore would have been better on defense if Humphrey played. He's not the same player he was four or five years ago. But the fact is his replacement Chidobe Awuzie gave up a touchdown pass. And Baltimore allowed 35 points or more for only the third time this season while Carolina quarterback Bryce Young delivered his fourth-best passer rating of the season. "At the end of the day we had a lead, we were on the field with a lead," coach Jesse Minter said. "We didn't hold it." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Humphrey's suspension surely changed the subject about this season for the Ravens for a couple of days last week. But the team that could not abide Humphrey's words better get used to much uglier things said about them in the coming days. Some fringe (I think) Ravens fans spent time on social media both wondering about and calling for Minter to be fired after only one season. His agreement to suspend Humphrey didn't protect the coach from fans that care more about good results than good intentions. Considering this was a team expected to compete for a postseason berth when the season began, this is now one of the club's most disappointing seasons in recent memory. articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton is known for his arm strength, and he may have just revealed his secret to helping him control it.

In the postgame press conference following the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, Milton was asked what he does before hurling a deep pass.

articles.body: Being associated with one of the NFL's biggest stars brought Kayla Nicole plenty of attention, but not all of it came with support. The media personality, who previously dated Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, has faced years of public commentary about her personal life. Now, she is making it clear that other people's opinions no longer define her. In an exclusive conversation with OK!, Nicole opened up about self-confidence, online criticism and the importance of protecting her peace while building a career that goes far beyond her high-profile relationship.Kayla Nicole addresses public scrutiny after Travis Kelce relationshipKayla Nicole's past relationship with Kelce has kept her name connected to the NFL star long after their romance ended. Kelce later began dating Taylor Swift, turning his personal life into a major subject of public fascination. As a result, Nicole has often found herself pulled into online conversations about her former boyfriend and his relationship.However, she appears determined not to let public opinion dictate how she lives. The Tennessee Titans defense continued to struggle as the team suffered a 51-30 loss against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday at AT&T Stadium.

Tennessee became the first team in the Super Bowl era to allow 40-plus points and 450-plus total yards in three consecutive games, according to CBS Sports writer Doug Clawson .

The Titans allowed 43 points and 510 yards during an overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. After a bye in Week 9, they surrendered 40 points and 459 yards against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Cowboys compiled 480 total yards in Sunday's rout.

The defensive struggles are particularly concerning considering first-year head coach Robert Saleh has a defensive background. Still, there is some reason for optimism.

In Saleh's first year as head coach, the New York Jets finished last in the NFL in total defense. He helped transform the unit into one of the league's best, as it ranked in the top five in yards allowed in each of the next four seasons.

The Titans picked up its first win of the 2026 season in Week 6 against the hapless Indianapolis Colts, but they weren't able to build any positive momentum. Tennessee has lost its four games since that victory, falling to a 1-9 record.

Philadelphia Eagles star running back spent the end of Sunday's 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on the sideline, calling into question just how injured he may have been after leaving the game with a left shoulder or arm issue.

Following the contest, he didn't offer much more insight into the situation but said he believes he'll be good to go for Thanksgiving's matchup against the Dallas Cowboys:

Steelers' Historic Losing Streak vs. Eagles

Barkley, 29, had an excellent game, rushing 17 times for 75 yards and a touchdown, including a 38-yard scoring scamper in the first quarter that propelled the Eagles to a 13-0 lead.

It was the third-most rushing yards he's had this season—he's yet to eclipse 100 rushing yards on the year—as Philly's offense has struggled and a once-mighty run game has stalled.

Injuries to both Barkley and the offensive line haven't helped matters. The star running back has dealt with a number of injuries throughout the season, missing two games and leaving another two early due to injury issues.

Even coming into Sunday's game, he told reporters he wasn't completely healthy and noted that "everybody is going through something."

"I wish the bye week was like a magic pill and everything vanishes, but that's only in La La Land, I guess," he added over the weekend. "But it definitely did help. It felt really good, when you're battling injuries and especially fighting through injuries, your body reacts a certain way. You compensate a little bit. It felt good to take a week off, but it's not really a week off. You're still doing stuff throughout the body to keep yourself fresh. But I feel good and ready for the week."

Unfortunately for the Eagles, he couldn't get through the game without picking up another knock, though he sounded optimistic about being available for Thursday's rivalry matchup with the Cowboys.

articles.title: Chiefs and Bills take care of business ahead of the NFL’s biggest regular-season game
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs beat Arizona 34-7 and the Buffalo Bills handled Miami 26-9 to set up a Thanksgiving showdown in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed.
articles.body: Sunday in the NFL felt a little like November in the SEC for the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills. You know how SEC teams like to schedule a late-season cupcake as a tune-up before the big rivalry game? Well, the Chiefs and Bills don’t get to pick their opponents, but whoever put together the Week 11 schedule did them both a favor. When I wrote about the Week 11 betting lines Thursday, Buffalo was favored by 16.5 points and Kansas City by 15.5. Both covered those numbers. The Bills beat the Miami Dolphins, 26-9, while the Chiefs demolished the Arizona Cardinals, 34-7. Of course, the analogy only works if the cupcake leads into a big rivalry game. And that’s exactly what’s in store for NFL fans on Thanksgiving night, when Patrick Mahomes and the 8-2 Chiefs head to Buffalo to face Josh Allen and the 9-1 Bills. The Bills have never hosted a game on Thanksgiving, and for their first one, they get the biggest game of the NFL regular season. Sure, Chiefs-Bills doesn’t have the history of Steelers-Browns, Cowboys-Eagles or Packers-Lions. But try telling someone in Buffalo that Kansas City isn’t a rival. Mahomes and Allen met in the playoffs four times in five seasons, twice with a trip to the Super Bowl on the line. The Chiefs ended the Bills’ season all four times. And I’m guessing nobody in Buffalo needs me to explain what "13 seconds" means. DK METCALF DISQUALIFIED FROM STEELERS GAME FOR UNSPORTSMANLIKE PENALTIES INCLUDING POKING OPPONENT'S FACEMASK Kansas City certainly looked ready Sunday. Travis Kelce had a vintage Kelce game, catching six passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns, both before halftime. Mahomes threw for 324 yards and three scores, and rookie running back Emmett Johnson added 105 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That’s three straight games with at least 34 points for the Chiefs. Buffalo, meanwhile, won by 17 on a day when Allen threw two interceptions and didn’t run the ball once. How often do you get to say that about a Bills win? Allen still threw for 304 yards, and Miami managed three field goals. I wouldn’t count on Mahomes being quite that accommodating. Thanksgiving night could decide where the Chiefs and Bills meet in January The Bills have won five straight regular-season games against the Chiefs. A sixth would put Buffalo at 10-1, two games ahead of Kansas City. If the Chiefs win, they’ll close out Thanksgiving night tied with Buffalo at 9-2 and holding the head-to-head tiebreaker. That’s a pretty big swing for a Bills team trying to earn the AFC’s No. 1 seed for the first time in the Josh Allen era. Allen has won all three of his regular-season trips to Arrowhead and lost all three of his playoff games there. Mahomes has won in Buffalo in January, too, beating the Bills 27-24 in the divisional round after the 2023 season. But both times these two played for the AFC championship, Buffalo had to go to Kansas City. A win Thursday gives Allen a much better shot at making Mahomes get on a plane in late January. And if you’re wondering what happened the last time Buffalo did earn the No. 1 seed, the 1993 Bills won the AFC championship game at home, 30-13. The team they beat to get to the Super Bowl? The Kansas City Chiefs. BUFFALO BILLS TAP HOMETOWN HEROES GOO GOO DOLLS FOR THANKSGIVING NIGHT HALFTIME CONCERT Of course, the Bengals would prefer to host the AFC championship game themselves. They’re 7-2 heading into Monday Night Football against Washington, and I suspect they’ll be rooting for Kansas City on Thanksgiving. A Chiefs win would give Buffalo its second loss, and the Bengals don’t get a shot at the Bills in the regular season. They do, however, get the Chiefs at home on Dec. 13. And yes, the Broncos and Jaguars are in the mix for the No. 1 seed, too. Jacksonville even went into Cincinnati and beat the Bengals. But when I ranked my Super Bowl contenders at the halfway point, I had three AFC teams in the top tier. If it’s my money, I’m still betting the AFC runs through Kansas City, Buffalo or Cincinnati. So if the Chiefs win on Thanksgiving and the Bengals keep winning, Chiefs-Bengals on Dec. 13 might be the biggest game of the NFL regular season. That gives me about two weeks to ask my editor if changing "Bills" to "Bengals" and running this article again counts as plagiarizing myself. Chiefs-Bills headlines a much better Week 12 schedule Week 11 didn’t look particularly good on paper, and most of Sunday’s early games looked about the same on TV. If the NFL wants to wash the taste of those lopsided matchups out of our mouths, though, Week 12 ought to do it. The Packers visit the Rams on Wednesday night. The Bears and Lions open Thanksgiving with a game that could help decide the NFC North, and we get Seahawks-49ers on Sunday afternoon. I’d happily watch any of those three, and none is the game I’m looking forward to most. That would be Chiefs-Bills on Thanksgiving night. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD The only downside is that three of those four games will be over before we even get to Friday. Then again, am I really going to complain about only having to wait four days to see Mahomes and Allen play each other? Ask me again Sunday at 1 p.m. when I’m trying to decide which game gets the main TV in my living room and Saints-Bengals is probably my best option.

articles.title: Robert Saleh Calls Out Titans for 'Disgusting, Embarrassing Football' After 51-30 Loss to Cowboys
articles.summary: It's been another ugly season for the Tennessee Titans, and Sunday might have been the worst performance of all.
articles.body:
It's been another ugly season for the Tennessee Titans, and Sunday might have been the worst performance of all.

The Titans fell to the Dallas Cowboys 51-30 in what head coach Robert Saleh called a "disgusting, embarrassing" showing.

"It was disgusting, embarrassing football," Saleh told reporters . "That starts with me. I got to figure it out."

The Cowboys have one of the best offenses in the league, and they punished a lowly Titans' defense. Quarterback Dak Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns, with CeeDee Lamb hauling in 11 receptions for 132 yards and a touchdown and George Pickens bringing in seven receptions for 102 yards and a score.

Running backs Javonte Williams and KaVontae Turpin each found the end zone, and Prescott also rushed for a touchdown.

The Titans have given up 40 or more in each of their last three games, and they're on pace to give up 493 points this season, or an average of 29 points per game.

Struggling second-year quarterback Cam Ward actually put together a solid day with 248 passing yards and two touchdowns, but that was far from enough on a pitiful defensive day.

While the 1-9 Titans have virtually no chance of reaching the playoffs, Saleh is hoping that the ugly loss will make them "feel pissed" as they try to salvage what is left of the season.

"We have no choice but to get better," Saleh said. "I mean, sh--t, it can't get any worse."

articles.title: Jaguars lose third challenge on Parker Washington play that sure looked like a TD catch
articles.summary: The Jaguars were down to their final challenge against the Giants due to a previous blatant officiating error.
articles.body:
The NFL's replay assist system is intended to quickly correct obvious missed calls on the field so coaches don't have to challenge them.

During Sunday's game between the New York Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars, it had the exact opposite effect and cost Jacksonville a challenge.

And then when the Jaguars used their final challenge at a critical juncture in the fourth quarter, officials made a ruling that was questionable at best on what sure looked like a Jacksonville touchdown. The Giants went on to beat the Jaguars, 23-18 .

With the Jaguars trailing 20-6 early in the fourth quarter, Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington in the back left corner of the end zone.

Washington made what looked like a spectacular leaping catch in tight coverage while getting both feet down at the edge of the end zone.

But officials ruled it incomplete. Down to his last challenge, Jaguars coach Liam Coen challenged the ruling on the field. It was to no avail.

Officials looked at the play in slow motion and determined that Washington did not complete the catch. Referee Craig Wrolstad didn't offer much of an explanation when announcing the verdict.

"After review, it is an incomplete pass," Wrolstad said.

Washington initially bobbled the ball in the air, but secured control before either of his feet hit the turf. The ball moved in his hands as he hit the ground, but Washington didn't appear to lose his grasp of the ball at any point.

CBS officiating analyst Gene Steratore disagreed with the call on the field and from the replay crew.

"I do not think he lost possession of the football," Steratore said.

But Steratore didn't have a say in the matter, and the result of the play was a fourth down in which the Jaguars settled for a field goal to cut their deficit to 20-9.

Steratore later reported that the league office told him there wasn't "enough clear and obvious evidence" evidence to overturn the call on the field.

The Jaguars were down to their final challenge to begin with because of an obvious officiating error.

On the first play of the second quarter, Jaguars running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. gained 2 yards on third-and-2 for what should have been a first down. Officials on the field spotted the ball beyond the line to gain and signaled first-and-10. The chains were moved.

But a whistle blew before the Jaguars broke their huddle. Officials announced that replay assist determined that Rodriguez came up short. They moved the ball back short of the line to gain, and the chains moved back to their previous position.

The CBS broadcast then showed slow-motion replay of the run. Rodriguez clearly extended the ball beyond the line to gain before his right knee touched the ground. Coen agreed and threw his challenge flag.

After commercial break, the ball had been moved back to its original position. Replay determined that Rodriguez had reached the line to gain, and the Jaguars were correctly awarded a first down.

To recap: Officials got it right on the field. Replay assist incorrectly determined that the ball was short of the line to gain. Instant replay upon a Jaguars challenge determined that officials got it right in the first place and that replay assist screwed up.

Jaguars penalized for officiating mistake

The effective result of the replay assist error was the Jaguars burning a challenge. The challenge was the second of the day by Coen, and he was on the first two.

Because he got them both right, the Jaguars were awarded a third challenge that they used to challenge the would-be-Parker touchdown that was ultimately ruled incomplete. At that point, the Jaguars were out of challenges for the rest of the game.

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert entered the NFL's concussion protocol after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the New York Jets.

Herbert has played all six of his NFL seasons with the Bolts, who selected the ex-Oregon star with the sixth overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft. The Chargers largely struggled over Herbert's first four years save for a lone playoff appearance in 2022, although that wasn't the fault of the quarterback. Jim Harbaugh then arrived in town in 2024, and this team was much-improved in 2024 and 2025, going 11-6 with playoff appearances each season.
