articles.title: Broncos Beat Raiders, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Mendoza, Nix, Jeanty, Top Players
articles.summary: Jonah Coleman's hat trick led the Denver Broncos to a 38-24 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, despite a three-touchdown performance from Fernando Mendoza, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver on Sunday.
articles.body:
Jonah Coleman's hat trick led the Denver Broncos to a 38-24 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, despite a three-touchdown performance from Fernando Mendoza, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver on Sunday.

The Broncos entered the matchup against the Raiders as 10.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and secured the victory by 14 points behind 225 yards from Bo Nix and big defensive plays down the stretch.

In Mendoza's second start for the Raiders following the Nov. 10 trade that sent Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings, the former Heisman Trophy winner and No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft finished with an impressive three-touchdown performance, throwing for 267 yards but committing a costly pick-six late in the game that sealed the win for the Broncos.

The win improved Denver's record to 8-2 overall, 3-1 in divisional play and 4-1 in conference play, extending its winning streak to six games. The Broncos remain atop the AFC West alongside the Kansas City Chiefs, whom they have split the season series with.

Las Vegas fell to 4-7 overall, 1-2 in divisional play and 3-4 in conference play, remaining third in the AFC West.

Denver took a 3-0 lead after the opening quarter behind a 38-yard field goal from Wil Lutz.

Nix connected with tight end Adam Trautman before Jonah Coleman rushed in a score on back-to-back possessions to give the Broncos a 17-0 lead.

The Raiders notched a field goal and a touchdown before halftime, with Mendoza finding Ashton Jeanty for his first touchdown pass of the season. Las Vegas' defense then closed out the half with an interception off Nix as the clock wound down.

Las Vegas added a touchdown on a 19-yard pass from Mendoza to tight end Ian Thomas to tie the game at 17.

Denver answered on its next drive with Coleman's second rushing touchdown of the day, regaining the lead at 24-17 heading into the fourth quarter.

Coleman's third touchdown of the day came in the fourth quarter, stretching the Raiders' hopes of a comeback as he extended the Broncos' lead to 31-17.

Mendoza and the Raiders refused to go away, with the rookie quarterback finding Jack Bech for a 7-yard touchdown pass to make it a one-score game with 4:29 remaining.

The Raiders forced the Broncos into a three-and-out on their next drive, giving them a chance to tie the game on their next possession. However, Mendoza threw his first career interception, which Ja'Quan McMillian returned for a pick-six to put the game out of reach and extend Denver's lead to 38-24.

Denver will hit the road to face the Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday at 3 p.m. ET, while the Raiders will travel to face the Cleveland Browns next Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: George Kittle Pays Tribute to WWE's Penta With Mask in Video Ahead of 49ers-Vikings in Mexico City
articles.summary: Ahead of the San Francisco 49ers' Sunday Night Football game in Mexico City, tight end George Kittle paid homage to a friend.
articles.body:
Ahead of the San Francisco 49ers' Sunday Night Football game in Mexico City, tight end George Kittle paid homage to a friend.

Heading into the contest against the Minnesota Vikings, Kittle donned the mask of WWE star Penta, who is from Mexico.

It's not the first time Kittle has shown his support for Penta. In February, 2025, he joined his friend in the ring during WWE's RAW show in Nashville.

Kittle joined Penta during WrestleMania weekend in New Orleans in 2018 after watching Penta wrestle multiple matches and visiting his locker room to introduce himself, where they swapped a jersey for a mask.

Now, Kittle sometimes celebrates touchdowns with a hand gesture representing "Cero Miedo," which means "zero fear" and comes from Penta's performances in the ring.

articles.title: NFL Week 11 Winners and Losers: Steelers have another horrible loss, and it seems obvious how their season will end
articles.summary: The Steelers looked bad in a loss to the Eagles, who had lost seven in a row.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are likely going to the playoffs. But they also appear very likely to be headed toward being one-and-done, if they do make the postseason.

The Steelers have been one-and-done in the playoffs six straight times and the way they're playing lately doesn't give much confidence that they can get out of the wild-card round this time either.

Losing to the Cincinnati Bengals is excusable, though it was troubling how badly they got blown out. But nobody should be losing to this season's Philadelphia Eagles. The Eagles, who had lost seven in a row, beat the Steelers 19-16 . Philadelphia was led by Joe Milton III, its third quarterback of the season. Milton didn't play well, throwing for just 141 yards, but the Steelers still couldn't outscore the Eagles.

Not only was there the loss, but the entire DK Metcalf experience somehow continued to get worse. Metcalf was getting into it with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean throughout the game and then poked DeJean in the eye after a play in the third quarter. That dirty act got Metcalf ejected and the NFL will certainly look into a suspension . It's not like it matters given how little production Metcalf has given Pittsburgh this season and pretty much through his entire Steelers tenure, but it still had to be infuriating for Pittsburgh to be stuck with fewer than 10 points and then watch its supposed No. 1 receiver walking back to the locker room after being kicked out. It is turning out to be a disastrous trade for Pittsburgh.

"This is definitely a game we expected to win … we need him in those games," Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy told the media afterward. "That's not acceptable to get thrown out of a game."

It was a miserable day overall for the Steelers. They couldn't get the run game going, so they abandoned it. Their leading rusher was Aaron Rodgers, with 29 yards. Their top two backs, Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle, combined for 43 yards on 14 carries. Rodgers continues to fade as he creeps up on his 43rd birthday. He has been good for his age but expecting him to continue to play at an above-average pace all season was always wishful thinking.

Rodgers had 227 yards and a touchdown, but the touchdown came late with the Steelers trailing by 10 points. That was the only time Pittsburgh got in the end zone. The rest of the season might not be pretty, and it will come with more of Rodgers ranting against everyone around him.

The defense wasn't bad, but when it needed a stop on third-and-6 in the final minutes, Milton found DeVonta Smith for the game-clinching first down. Pittsburgh also gave up a 38-yard touchdown run to Saquon Barkley that was Philadelphia's only TD on Sunday.

Steelers fans have to be wondering how they can get off the hamster wheel. Every season seems about the same. The Steelers pull off some unlikely wins, and their record is just good enough to get into the playoffs. Then they get to the postseason and get blown out. Their last five playoff losses have come by double digits.

The Steelers had a coaching change, going from Mike Tomlin to McCarthy, and nothing has really changed. They're probably good enough to make the playoffs in a weak AFC wild-card race. And there aren't any signs the last couple weeks that they're able to go on the road and upset a team like Jacksonville or Denver in the wild-card round or even keep the game close. And perhaps the Steelers, at 6-4, could fade in the wild-card race, considering their next three games are against Denver, Houston and Jacksonville.

It was another rough Sunday for the Steelers. Being a likely playoff team should be something to get excited about, but it's hard when the endgame now seems obvious.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 11 of the NFL season:

Jonah Coleman: The Denver Broncos didn't trade for running back Jonathan Taylor or any other big-name at the trading deadline, and that might be for the best.

Denver could have a late-season star at RB. Rookie Jonah Coleman, a fourth-round pick, had a huge day as the Broncos held off the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 . Coleman had 111 rushing yards and three touchdowns in the win. Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza had a good game with three touchdowns, but threw a pick-6 with 1:52 left and the Raiders trailing by seven points.

Coleman got positive reviews in camp but suffered an ankle injury early in the season. He had an opportunity when he came back to carve out a big role due to JK Dobbins' ineffectiveness and RJ Harvey's knee injury, and he has been coming along each week before Sunday's breakout.

With the Broncos at 8-2 and facing a very easy schedule the rest of the way, Coleman could be a big story over the second half of the season.

Josh Johnson: It didn't matter if the Arizona Cardinals beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. Johnson's story was a great one either way.

Johnson got the start for the Cardinals when Carson Beck's back injury kept him out of practice during the week. The 40-year-old made some history on his first snap, as the second-oldest non-specialist to play for the Cardinals, behind only Jim Thorpe , who played one game at age 41 for the Chicago Cardinals in 1928.

And Johnson, who has played for 15 teams, threw a touchdown in the first half, the 15th of his long and strange career. Johnson was reasonable, with 155 yards and that touchdown.

Predictably, the Cardinals couldn't keep up with the Chiefs. Kansas City got another big game from rookie Emmett Johnson, who had 105 yards rushing and 38 more receiving as Kenneth Walker III got another week off to nurse a groin injury. It was no surprise the Chiefs won 34-7 . But even in the loss, Johnson playing and doing OK at 40 years old was fun to see.

Bills' defense: At some point Buffalo will face a tough offense. It has had a few weeks of playing against bad offenses with backup quarterbacks. But let's give the Bills credit for handling business.

Buffalo's defense did its job Sunday, holding down the Miami Dolphins led by quarterback Kyle McCord. The Bills won 26-9 , allowing just 185 yards and no touchdowns.

The Bills' defense was not very good to start the season, bringing into question whether Buffalo was good enough on that side of the ball to win a Super Bowl. The Bills won't get to see quarterbacks like Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz and McCord in the playoffs, so we don't know for sure if their defense has turned a corner. At least it's better than struggling against those quarterbacks.

Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb: Most of the focus for the Dallas Cowboys this season has been on their awful defense. That defense is a shame because it is wasting another good season of Prescott's prime.

Prescott was very good in a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday , as he has been most of the season. Prescott threw for 325 yards and four touchdowns including one to Lamb, who had another big game. Lamb had 11 catches for 132 yards.

The Cowboys' defense might have been slightly better Sunday, with Mike Pettine taking over play-calling from Christian Parker. But it was the type of game the Cowboys are going to have to keep winning if they want to stay in the NFC East race, with the offense scoring enough to not make the defense's struggles matter. Prescott is capable of making it happen.

Jaguars' chances at a No. 1 seed: The one thing Jacksonville hadn't done this season was take a truly bad loss. The Jaguars lost to the Broncos and fell against the Texans in the final seconds in London, which was a reasonable defeat.

The New York Giants, who lead the NFC East, might not be a bad loss either. But it felt like one Sunday.

The Jaguars played by far their worst game of the season and the Giants won 23-18 . The Jaguars were very quiet on offense until the fourth quarter and that's what ultimately cost them the game, but there were a couple turning points in the fourth quarter that will be discussed. Jacksonville had what appeared to be a Parker Washington touchdown catch but it was called incomplete when it was ruled he didn't have control and both feet in. That looked like the wrong call.

Then with less than four minutes left and the Jaguars trailing by eight points, they opted for a 26-yard field goal on fourth-and-goal at the 8-yard line. That decision to kick instead of going for it was questionable and the Jaguars never got the ball back.

The Jaguars were in the mix for the No. 1 seed but that gets a lot tougher now that they're two losses behind the Bills. It was set to be a hot competition for the conference's only bye and the Jaguars will have trouble making up that ground.

Los Angeles Chargers, for now: In the long run, the Chargers will appreciate losing Sunday.

In the moment, it was embarrassing. The New York Jets had lost eight of their last nine games, but sliced through the Chargers' defense in a 27-24 win . The Jets scored on each of their first five possessions, then ran out the clock after a late Chargers touchdown.

The Chargers got their first win this season in Week 10, so the real pressure is off. The only real drama left for the Chargers is if they can get the first pick of the draft . The Chargers, Titans and Dolphins are the three teams tied at the bottom of the NFL with just one win each. Losing to the Jets, a strong contender to finish with the worst record in the NFL, will pay off in April. That's probably worth the shame of losing to the Jets at home Sunday.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers: It's not like the Buccaneers were expected to win Sunday in Detroit. But maybe that's the problem.

The Buccaneers, like everyone else in the NFC South, seem incapable of beating a good opponent. Tampa Bay hung around for a while against Detroit, but the Lions eventually wore the Bucs out in a 31-21 win . Jahmyr Gibbs continued his fantastic season for the Lions with 118 total yards and two touchdowns.

Tampa Bay could still win the division because nobody else is running away with it. But at 3-7, it's not like the Buccaneers deserve a playoff spot.

Jesse Minter: Not all of the Baltimore Ravens' struggles this season are Minter's fault. But he's not having a great first season as head coach.

Minter's defense failed again Sunday. The Panthers put up 378 yards and won 35-33 . Carolina drove at the end for a go-ahead field goal and Jacoby Brissett was picked off on a deflected pass. Brissett, however, wasn't the biggest problem. He had 276 yards and a touchdown. It's that nothing else was great for the Ravens, especially the defense. It was another blown lead for the Ravens, which has been a theme of their season.

"At the end of the day we had a lead, and we didn't hold it," Minter said . "So I'll take responsibility for that."

The Ravens are a perennial contender but that status is fading. Baltimore (4-7) lost its sixth in a row.

Minter might be a good coach over time, but there has to be skepticism after Baltimore's fade this season.

Kellen Moore: Could Moore be in trouble as New Orleans Saints head coach?

The Saints lost 21-13 to the Chicago Bears , and while that is a tough opponent, it's not like New Orleans has done much to impress this season. The Saints (3-7) haven't looked good all season. Tyler Shough hasn't progressed in his second season, though he's not getting a ton of help. The Saints' hot streak late last season, after a 1-8 start, seems like a mirage due to catching a very easy part of the schedule.

Team owner Gayle Benson had some startling comments earlier this season that seemed to be critical of Moore and the front office as well. She later said she endorsed Moore. But the losses are piling up.

articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 11 Results, Who Could Titans & Jets Take?
articles.summary: There's a clear three-team race for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft after Week 11's Sunday afternoon games.
articles.body:
There's a clear three-team race for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft after Week 11's Sunday afternoon games.

The Tennessee Titans, Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins all sit at 1-9. The Titans are ahead of the other two top-pick competitors on the strength of schedule tiebreaker.

The New York Jets are two games ahead of those three teams in the win column, but they'll still be a major player in the first round.

New York currently owns the Nos. 4 and 5 overall picks in the projected order.

The No. 4 overall pick was traded to the Jets in the Sauce Gardner deal with the Indianapolis Colts. It also has the 15th overall pick from the Quinnen Williams trade with the Dallas Cowboys.

4. New York Jets (via Indianapolis - 3-8)

24. Philadelphia (via Jacksonville - 7-2)

If the Titans are committed to Cam Ward, they have to land Jeremiah Smith with the No. 1 overall pick.

Ward's improved in recent weeks with three straight 200-yard passing games. He threw for multiple touchdowns in each of those contests.

The Titans offense is limited, though, on top-tier pass-catching talent to take Ward's numbers to a higher level.

Carnell Tate needs a running mate, like his former Ohio State teammate, to really take the Titans offense to the next level.

On Sunday, Chimere Dike and Calvin Ridley led the Titans with 69 and 68 receiving yards, but imagine what Ward could've done against the Dallas Cowboys defense with Tate and Smith running around the secondary.

It's a no-brainer pick for the Titans, if they remain in the top spot. They can figure out their defensive woes either in free agency, or in the latter rounds of the draft.

Any of the teams beneath the Titans in the projected raft order would love to have Smith's talent in their offense as well.

The Chargers would almost certainly take Smith to provide Justin Herbert with a true No. 1 target.

The Jets, Dolphins and others would have more difficult decisions to make on Smith because of their quarterback needs.

Everyone is aware by now that the 2027 quarterback class isn't what it was made out to be at the start of the football season.

Darian Mensah appears to be the safest of the signal-callers to pick at the top of the first round because of his experience.

Mensah is one of the more polished quarterbacks in the draft class, and he just clinched his second straight spot in the ACC Championship Game. He played in that game with the Duke Blue Devils last year and will do so with the Miami Hurricanes in two weeks.

Mensah's numbers have taken a small hit without Malachi Toney on the field in the last two weeks, but he still ranks third in the FBS in touchdown passes and fourth in passing yards.

If the Titans moved on from Ward, they'd have to land a more experienced player, like Mensah, so they could turn things around quickly.

The Jets should be intrigued by Mensah as well because he'd be a good fit inside an offense that features stars at the offensive skill positions.

The Dolphins might be more inclined to go after more of a developmental prospect, like Drew Mestemaker, because of what stage they're at in their rebuild.

But for the Titans and Jets, Mensah has to be at, or near, the top of the list.

NFL Teams That Could Trade Up for Jeremiah Smith 📈

Not much has been made about the top defensive prospects in the draft class because of Smith and the quarterbacks.

However, there are a few defensive players that have the potential to land inside the top five.

South Carolina EDGE Dylan Stewart will be in contention to be the top defender picked.

Stewart's overall body of work at South Carolina is impressive. He's recorded nine forced fumbles and 13.5 sacks.

The Titans should go offense with their first-round pick, but in the situation where they don't, Stewart should be high of their draft board.

The Jets are one of the top potential suitors for Stewart because of their volume of draft picks and need for more pass-rushers. Stewart and David Bailey could be one of the best young pass-rushing tandems in the sport.

articles.title: Week 12 Waiver Wire Breakout Fantasy Football Pickups from Sunday's Box Scores
articles.summary: If the whopping six NFL teams on bye in Week 11 of the season didn't inject chaos into your fantasy lineup, then mounting injuries around the league almost certainly did. However, Week 11 is nearly in the books, and if you're on track to record an L, it's time to put your energy into making smart waiver wire claims for Week 12.
articles.body:
If the whopping six NFL teams on bye in Week 11 of the season didn't inject chaos into your fantasy lineup, then mounting injuries around the league almost certainly did. However, Week 11 is nearly in the books, and if you're on track to record an L, it's time to put your energy into making smart waiver wire claims for Week 12.

With Thanksgiving, the holiday the late John Madden thought was as much about football as it was about family and food, almost upon us, there will be no byes to manage; every single team will play in Week 12. That gives you a cornucopia of players to choose from on waivers this week and hope that your team can either keep a winning streak going or turn things around with your full roster (sans injuries) available to you.

Let's take a look at three players who stood out in fantasy in Week 11. Points use PPR scoring and rostered percentages are via FantasyPros .

Week 11 stats: 6 att, 69 rush yds, 1 rush TD, 4 rec, 27 rec yds, 17.6 pts

With Jacoby Brissett under center, the Baltimore Ravens offense is looking more and more enticing for fantasy managers. Multiple Ravens had great fantasy days on Sunday, including running back Justice Hill.

While there's no question Derrick Henry is still the lead back in Baltimore, Hill has increasingly shown a nose for explosive plays as well as an ability to gain yardage in the passing game. In Sunday's loss to the Carolina Panthers, Hill strung together a 19-yard touchdown run and another 36-yard breakaway play. This is his second consecutive week with 10 or more fantasy points.

Henry was evaluated for a concussion after exiting Sunday's game but later cleared. While Hill won't be carrying any of Henry's normal workload in Week 12, he's still proving he can make a contribution worthy of FLEX consideration.

Week 11 stats: 5 rec, 56 rec yds, 2 rec TD, 22. 6 pts

If you're comfortable with your bench depth heading into Week 12 and you're looking for a high-upside player on waivers to stash for a potential future payoff, consider Buccaneers wideout Ted Hurst.

Hurst is volatile. Sunday's 22.6-point outing, which placed him at No. 3 among all fantasy wideouts by the end of the Sunday late afternoon slate, is nevertheless an outlier; Hurst has only had one other double-digit point game this year, in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. That's also the only other game this season in which he's found the end zone.

But Hurst was targeted seven times on Sunday, which led all Bucs receivers, for a 22.6% target share. On the other hand, in the three games before Week 11, he didn't record a single catch. If you have the luxury of claiming a speculative bench stash, Hurst is worth keeping an eye on.

Week 11 stats: 6 rec, 69 rec yds, 1 rush att, 4 rush yds, 1 fum, 13.3 pts

With Titans wideout Wan'Dale Robinson on injured reserve, targets have opened up in the Tennessee offense for Chimere Dike, Carnell Tate and Elic Ayomanor. Second-year quarterback Cam Ward has increased his passing volume and yardage over the last three games, with his attempts per game up to 36.6 from 29.7 across his first seven appearances.

Dike is one of the players who has been benefiting from this pass-heavy game script. His seven targets in Week 11 were his most of the season, and he responded with a season-high six receptions and his second-highest yardage on the season with 69.

Still, the Titans receiver room is crowded, and Dike has not yet become a consistent enough contributor to warrant FLEX consideration. He's a speculative stash ahead of Week 12.

articles.title: Broncos hold off Raiders with 3 Jonah Coleman TDs, late pick-6 of Fernando Mendoza
articles.summary: An AFC West clash headlines the afternoon game slate in Week 11.
articles.body: The Broncos leaned on Jonah Coleman's running and did just enough to slow down Fernando Mendoza in Denver's 38-24 victory at Empower Field at Mile High.Coleman ran for 111 yards and three scores, helping boost Denver to a 17-0 first-half lead and then keeping the Broncos in front with scores on back-to-back possessions in the second half. Mendoza threw three TD passes in his second NFL start, but with two minutes remaining, he was intercepted by the Broncos' Ja'Quan McMillian, who ran it back 35 yards for a back-breaking pick-6.What a snag by Ja'Quan McMillian 🔥LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2niarbeNHE— NFL (@NFL) November 23, 2026 The Broncos moved to 8-2 in first place in the AFC West, with tiebreakers putting them ahead of the 8-2 Chiefs for now. The Raiders' fourth-straight loss dropped them to 4-7 and 0-2 since Mendoza took over for Kirk Cousins. The Raiders, who were without tight end Brock Bowers, fought until the end. Mendoza led the Raiders on three straight scoring drives to tie the game at 17-17, making several impressive throws before coming up short.It was also Ashton Jeanty's best game of the season, totaling 169 yards from scrimmage and hauling in Mendoza's first TD pass in the NFL — a 68-yard catch and run on a wheel route. But the Broncos' defense firmed up when it needed to, forcing a turnover on downs early in the fourth quarter and running back the defensive score. Denver sacked Mendoza five times, hit him 11 times and had five of his passes batted down, including three by Zach Allen.Mendoza finished the game 18-of-37 passing for 267 yards, three TDs and the one pick.The Broncos took a 3-0 lead after A.J. Cole's punt appeared to be affected, traveling only 2 yards. They then scored touchdowns on consecutive drives to take a 17-0 edge, with Bo Nix hitting Adam Trautman on a 1-yard TD and Coleman's first score. The Coleman TD was set up by a pretty Nix-to-Marvin Mims pass on a flea flicker.🚨 FLEA FLICKER 🚨📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/0t6uLHiXUt— Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 22, 2026 Nix finished the game 19-of-35 passing for 225 yards with one TD and one pick. The interception came on an end-of-half heave into the end zone.But the Broncos left some meat on the bone at the end of the half, and the Raiders capitalized. Mendoza's first NFL touchdown pass was a beauty to Jeanty, who was matched up on Broncos linebacker Que Robinson.The Raiders had a touchdown nullified on offensive pass interference, and they ended up settling for a field goal, trailing 17-10 at halftime. It could have been a bigger Denver lead, but Nix's pass to a wide-open Troy Franklin hit off Franklin's helmet. What should have been a 58-yard TD ended up in zero points.After stopping the Broncos on fourth down on their opening drive of the third quarter, the Raiders struck back to tie it at 17-all on a well-designed TD pass to Ian Thomas. The Broncos answered with a 10-play, 72-yard TD drive on Coleman's second score. Then after the Raiders were stopped on fourth down, Coleman capped another TD drive to put Denver up two scores.Mendoza had another touchdown pass nullified when he was ruled past the line of scrimmage. But he found Jack Bech for a score to cut Denver's lead to 31-24. After the Raiders' defense earned a stop, Mendoza had one last shot. Just after the two-minute warning, McMillian jumped Mendoza's pass and ran it back for the game-changing score.

articles.title: Jaguars stunned by Giants amid officiating controversy, questionable late-game decision from head coach Liam Coen
articles.summary: Plagued by red zone woes, officiating controversy and a questionable late-game decision by Liam Coen, the Jaguars fell 23-18 to the Giants.
articles.body: The Jacksonville Jaguars entered Sunday at 7-2 having emerged as a Super Bowl favorite out of the AFC. The New York Giants doused them with a splash of cold water. Plagued by red-zone woes, officiating controversy and a questionable late-game decision by Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen, the Jaguars fell 23-18 to the Giants. Coen settles for FG and Jags don't see the ball againJacksonville had a shot to tie the game with fourth-and-goal at the New York 8-yard line and 3:40 remaining on the clock. New York led 23-15, and the Jaguars were down to one timeout. But instead of going for a potential game-tying touchdown and 2-point conversion, Coen opted to kick a field goal that cut the deficit to five points, apparently betting on the Jaguars' defense to get them the ball back. Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars suffered a stunning loss to the Giants on Sunday.IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERSThey did not. Cam Skattebo ran for a first down before the two-minute warning with the Jaguars having exhausted their final timeout. The Giants were able to kneel out the remaining two minutes of game clock in victory formation.It added up to a jarring loss for the now 7-3 Jaguars on the heels of an aggressive trade deadline in which they made several big swings to bolster their hopes of a Super Bowl run. The Giants, meanwhile, improved to 6-3-1 to maintain their lead in the NFC East over the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys.The Giants were in control virtually from the start. They took a 10-3 advantage into the second quarter and a 20-6 lead into halftime. While J.J. McCarthy kept New York's offense moving and scoring, the Jaguars repeatedly broke down in the red zone. Jacksonville's first three trips to the red zone produced 6 points courtesy of two field goals and a turnover on downs in the third quarter when a fourth-and-1 pass from Trevor Lawrence fell incomplete. Was this a catch?Jacksonville's fourth red-zone trip produced controversy on a third-down effort to cut their deficit to one possession. They appeared to do just that when Parker Washington made a leaping catch in the back of the end zone and got both feet in bounds. But officials ruled that he didn't maintain control of the ball as he hit the ground.Should this have been ruled a touchdown for the Jaguars?? Refs ruled it an incomplete pass after a lengthy review pic.twitter.com/6IwoyKIXrL— Rate the Refs (@Rate_the_Refs) November 23, 2026 Coen used Jacksonville's last remaining challenge to challenge the call on the field. The ball moved in Washington's hands after Washington hit the ground, but he never appeared to lose control of it. But officials didn't see enough to overturn the call on the field, and the ruling of an incomplete pass stood. The result was a fourth down in which the Jaguars settled for a field goal to cut their deficit to 20-9.Jacksonville finally cracked the end zone with a touchdown pass from Lawrence to Brian Thomas Jr. with 6:39 remaining. A failed 2-point conversion left the Jaguars facing a 23-15 hole.Then came the decision that will prompt plenty of questions for Coen. Why didn't Jags go for the TD?The Jaguars forced a 3-and-out punt on the ensuing Giants possession, then marched 60 yards to the New York 8-yard line. With one timeout remaining on fourth down, Coen faced a choice: Go for it with a chance to tie the game or kick the field goal and hope to get the ball back still in need of a touchdown. He opted to kick the field goal, and that ultimately sealed Jacksonville's fate. The Giants never gave the ball back.In the end, the Jaguars woke up on offense and limited the Giants on defense as they outgained New York, 354 yards to 238. Lawrence completed 25 of 47 passes for 301 yards with 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions. McCarthy completed 18 of 38 passes for 173 yards with 1 touchdown. But he didn't turn the ball over as the Giants won the takeaway battle, 2 to 1.The result will leave the Jaguars with plenty to ponder ahead of a Week 12 home game against the Titans.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy's Giants Stun Jaguars, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Lawrence, Skattebo, Top Players
articles.summary: The New York Giants stunned the Jacksonville Jaguars with a 23-18 victory on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.
articles.body:
The New York Giants stunned the Jacksonville Jaguars with a 23-18 victory on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.

The Jaguars entered the game as 5.5-point betting favorites on FanDuel Sportsbook , but the talent gap on the field didn't seem nearly as large as it did on paper.

Jacksonville entered Sunday's game on a three-game winning streak, averaging 38.3 points per game over the span. New York made it difficult for Jacksonville to find any offensive rhythm as the Giants defense applied consistent pressure on Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence.

Steelers' Historic Losing Streak vs. Eagles

Here's a look at the top performers from both teams:

Jacksonville kick returner Ameer Abdullah began the game with a 47-yard return on the opening kickoff, but they were ultimately held to three points after a sack by Giants defensive tackle D.J. Reader.

Giants cornerback Deonte Banks intercepted Lawrence on Jacksonville's second drive, allowing New York to tie the game with a 53-yard field goal by rookie kicker Dominic Zvada.

Giants defensive tackle Abdul Carter sacked Lawrence to hold the Jaguars to a three-and-out. New York's offense put together a seven-play, 53-yard drive that ended with quarterback Jameis Winston pushing his way into the end zone on fourth down.

Jacksonville put together a solid drive, but it nearly resulted in disaster after a strip-sack by Carter. Although Lawrence recovered his own fumble, the Jaguars were held to a field goal on their second red zone trip.

Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy extended New York's lead with an 8-yard touchdown to star wide receiver Malik Nabers in the second quarter.

Jacksonville's offense stalled after another drive-killing sack by Carter, and New York went into halftime with a 20-6 lead following Zvada's 54-yard field goal.

The third quarter was sloppy by both teams. Zvada, who scored on field goals from 53 and 54 yards in the first half, missed a 32-yard attempt on New York's first drive of the second half. The Jaguars punted the ball away after mustering just one yard on their first drive of the quarter.

Jacksonville had an opportunity to cut into the deficit after defensive end Josh Hines-Allen forced a fumble by Giants running back Cam Skattebo, but the Jaguars came away empty-handed on a failed fourth-down attempt.

Jacksonville scored a field goal at the start of the fourth quarter, but it didn't take long for New York to get those points right back. Giants cornerback Paulson Adebo intercepted Lawrence, and Zvada drilled a 43-yard field goal to give New York a 23-9 lead.

The Jaguars finally scored their first touchdown with Lawrence finding wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. in the end zone for an 18-yard touchdown.

Jacksonville was able to cut into the deficit as the Giants' offense began to stall late in the fourth quarter. The Jaguars made it a one-score game with a 26-yard field goal, but it was too little, too late. New York kept the ball on the ground with Skattebo and ran out the clock.

Both teams entered Sunday's matchup atop their respective divisions. The Giants improved to a 6-3-1 record and appear to be on track to win the NFC East in their first season under head coach John Harbaugh. The Jaguars fell to 7-3, but they hold a comfortable lead for the AFC South title.

The Giants will face the Indianapolis Colts next week, while the Jaguars will return home for a divisional matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: New Tarik Skubal Rumors Reveal Blue Jays Contract Offer Before Mets' Historic $450M Deal
articles.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays lost the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes to the New York Mets on Sunday, but it wasn't from a lack of a substantial offer.
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays lost the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes to the New York Mets on Sunday, but it wasn't from a lack of a substantial offer.

According to Mitch Bannon of The Athletic, the Blue Jays offered Skubal a nine-year deal for just over $400 million, but it ultimately wasn't enough to beat the Mets' nine-year, $450 million deal.

The Mets deal set the record for the largest contract ever for a pitcher, and the Blue Jays' would've done the same. Toronto's offer also would've been the second-largest contract in franchise history, just behind Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s 14-year, $500 million contract.

Mets’ reported initial Tarik Skubal offer

Toronto missed the postseason in 2026 after reaching the World Series in 2025, and the addition of Skubal certainly would have helped the rotation try to get back to the postseason next year. Still, the team has plenty of talent and is capable of another run like the one it made in 2025.

Along with the Mets and Blue Jays, the Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres were the two known teams also in the race for the two-time Cy Young Award winner. There was also at least one mystery team reportedly in the running for Skubal.

While the Dodgers hoped to retain Skubal after trading for him during the 2026 season, ESPN's Alden González reported that Los Angeles never actually made an offer to him because of "the uncertainty of a new CBA and what the economic model might look like."

Now, Skubal will join a Mets team that has been aggressive on the free agent market for years but still has little to show for it. With the addition of Skubal, New York now has $1.6 billion tied to four players (Skubal, Juan Soto, Bo Bichette and Francisco Lindor). How the Mets will approach the rest of free agency remains to be seen after giving out such a lofty deal.

But Skubal is well worth the money, so long as he stays healthy and continues to have success into his 30s. He's coming off another strong year in which he went 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA, a 0.96 WHIP and 186 strikeouts.

articles.title: “He's determined to be very good at what he does”: How Travis Kelce went from Parker Ehinger's college mentor to one of  his biggest supporter in Kansas City Chiefs
articles.summary: Before Travis Kelce became one of the Kansas City Chiefs' biggest stars, he was a senior at Cincinnati helping a younger teammate find his feet.
articles.body: Before Travis Kelce became one of the Kansas City Chiefs' biggest stars, he was a senior at Cincinnati helping a younger teammate find his feet. That teammate was Parker Ehinger, a redshirt freshman offensive lineman who would later join Kelce in Kansas City. Their connection went beyond sharing a college team. Kelce served as a mentor to Ehinger, and when the Chiefs drafted the lineman in 2016, he made sure his former teammate had someone to turn to.Ehinger got that reminder almost immediately after the draft call. Kelce had already sent him a text, welcoming him to Kansas City and asking him to get in touch once he arrived. It was a familiar voice waiting at the start of a new NFL chapter.Travis Kelce became a mentor to Parker Ehinger during their Cincinnati daysThe connection began in 2012. Kelce was a senior at the University of Cincinnati, while Ehinger was a redshirt freshman. Ehinger started 12 games and appeared in all 13 that season as the Bearcats finished 9-3 in the regular season before beating Duke in the Belk Bowl.Kelce knew what Ehinger brought to the offensive line because they spent nearly two seasons working together. In the May 4, 2016 interview with Chiefs.com, Kelce remembered their time on the field and the friendship they built away from it."That's my guy," Kelce said. "I spent an entire year and a half of just being with that guy and communicating with him every single play, and it's one of those things where in college, you bond so well off the field just because you're around each other all the time. That's one of my brothers from UC."Kelce also praised Ehinger's ability to move across the offensive line. "He was our right tackle our senior year, he moved all over," he said in the same interview. "He's an all-around player on the offensive line. He can play at least four of the five positions."He also backed Ehinger's character and football intelligence, saying he would fit into the locker room and describing him as a smart player.Ehinger remembered Kelce's influence, too. During a conference call with local reporters on April 30, 2016, after the Chiefs drafted him, he was asked about their communication."Travis actually just texted me about five minutes ago," Ehinger said. "He said he can't wait to see me and told me to hit him up right when I get in town."He then explained what Kelce meant to him at Cincinnati: "He was a good mentor to have when I was a redshirt freshman playing and he was a senior." Travis Kelce welcomed his former mentee after the Chiefs drafted himThe Chiefs selected Ehinger with the 105th overall pick in the fourth round of the 2016 NFL Draft. The rookie knew he had plenty to learn, particularly in Andy Reid's West Coast offence. But he was confident in his ability to adapt.During the April 30 conference call, Ehinger identified his biggest strength as his football intelligence."It's my football IQ," he said. "I can pick up in any system very quickly."He also made it clear that he wasn't going to demand a particular position. "Wherever they need me at, I'm happy to play anywhere," Ehinger said. He added that he was willing to take center snaps if the team needed him there because he wanted to compete for a starting position.Kelce had already spoken to him about the organisation, Reid and life in Kansas City. Ehinger confirmed that his former teammate had encouraged him to get in touch after arriving in town.In the May 4 Chiefs.com interview, Kelce also described the personality he remembered from college."He's a fun personality," Kelce said. "He doesn't take anything too seriously, just like I don't."He added that Ehinger was more well-mannered than him, before praising his determination to improve. "He's determined to be very good at what he does, so he takes the time to perfect his craft and be the best player that he can be."In Kelce's case, welcoming Ehinger wasn't just about adding another Bearcat to the roster. It was about looking out for a former teammate he still called his brother.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Giants' Cam Skattebo Explains Backflip Despite Plans to Stop Celebration After Hutchinson's Injury
articles.summary: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo celebrated his team's 23-18 upset over the Jacksonville Jaguars by doing something he said he said he wouldn't do again: a backflip.
articles.body:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo celebrated his team's 23-18 upset over the Jacksonville Jaguars by doing something he said he said he wouldn't do again: a backflip.

"I kind of thought about it, I wanted to give one last one to my fans," Skattebo told reporters after the game, per The Athletic . "But at the end of the day, when the energy calls for it, man, and I got to bring the juice to my team, and when I backflip, it brings juice to these guys. It shows them how much I care. I play with my heart and soul in this game. I care about everybody on this team. I play as hard as I possibly can every single snap, and when the energy is needed and is called for, it's second nature, so it's hard to hold back from."

Skattebo planned on retiring the backflip after watching Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson suffer a season-ending knee injury on a celebration, but he couldn't resist the urge after clinching New York's victory with a 5-yard run.

Hutchinson's right knee buckled after he jumped in the air to celebrate a sack during Detroit's 35-10 victory over the New England Patriots in Munich. The star pass rusher was placed on the injured reserve list with a torn ACL in his right knee.

Skattebo told reporters last Monday that he would stop celebrating with a backflip after seeing Hutchinson's injury.

"Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that,'" Skattebo said. "That ain't going to happen to me."

"Obviously, I don't want to do them because of the injury that happened, but it brings energy to this team," Skattebo added on Sunday. "If I have to do it because the energy's low and we have a good moment, then that's what's going to happen."

During a month in which a significant injury has caused concern, it's clear there isn't much that can stop Skattebo from flipping with joy. The second-year running back even attempted a backflip at Fanatics Fest in July, despite recovering from a fractured fibula, ruptured deltoid ligament and dislocated ankle that cut his rookie campaign short.

Skattebo finished the game with 14 carries for 34 rushing yards to go along with three receptions for 14 receiving yards.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Says Giants Offense Took Jaguars Opting for FG 'Personal' Before Game-Clinching Drive
articles.summary: With 3:43 left in the game, the Jacksonville Jaguars were down by 8. On a fourth down at the New York Giants' 8-yard line, though, they didn't go for the touchdown.
articles.body:
With 3:43 left in the game, the Jacksonville Jaguars were down by 8. On a fourth down at the New York Giants' 8-yard line, though, they didn't go for the touchdown.

The Giants, apparently, took it personally.

Jacksonville kicked a 26-yard field goal to make it 23-18 and never touched the ball again, as the Giants got the first downs they needed to run out the clock, making the Jaguars' gamble go wrong.

Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy said his team took it as a challenge after the Jaguars seemingly believed they could stop New York's struggling offense to get the ball back.

"As an offense? We took that personal," he said. "The prior drives, that was something that they felt comfortable with doing. We can't get in that position. We can't give them that confidence to go out there and kick that field goal."

Though it backfired for the Jaguars, the Giants didn't give them much to believe that their offense would come through. New York hadn't scored a touchdown since the first half, and McCarthy threw 18-for-38 with 173 yards.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo ignores his own backflip celebration retirement promise at end of Giants victory over Jaguars
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo vowed to retire his backflip celebration, then did one anyway after the New York Giants clinched their 23-18 win over Jacksonville.
articles.body: There are some things about Cam Skattebo that the New York Giants can definitely count on: he is going to bring energy, he's still in danger of fumbling and he should not be trusted when he says he's going to put the backflip on the back burner. Two of those three are not optimal. One of those three is really moronic. LIONS' STAR HURT CELEBRATING SACK OF PATRIOTS’ DRAKE MAYE AS BOTH INJURED ON POSSIBLY SEASON-ALTERING PLAY CAM SKATTEBO PUTTING HIS BACKFLIP ON THE BACK BURNER AFTER SEEING AIDAN HUTCHINSON CELEBRATION INJURY Days after telling reporters he was going to retire from his signature backflip celebration, Skattebo apparently decided to ignore everything he said (good advice for all of us, actually) and performed one of his semi-plyometric flights near the end of the Giants game on Sunday. "When energy calls for it, it calls for it," Skattebo boldly explained to reporters after the game. "My teammates, I do whatever I can to bring the energy for the team and play this game with my heart and soul. So when that happens, it's second nature. "It's hard to hold back." You want to know the dumb part about this explanation? Neither energy, nor the team were calling for Skattebo to perform a backflip at the moment he did. The Giants had clinched their 23-18 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars with two minutes to play when Skattebo delivered a 5-yard run. The game was effectively over. But that's when Skattebo forgot everything he said about not risking an injury the way he watched Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson did on Nov. 15 – which was by leaving his feet to perform a celebration. DAN CAMPBELL WON'T STOP PLAYERS FROM CELEBRATING EVEN AFTER STAR AIDAN HUTCHINSON WAS INJURED CELEBRATING Hutchinson, by the way, last week promised he's done going airborne. So, Skattebo did his unretired backflip when the game was decided. And wouldn't it have been utterly embarrassing if he'd done that backflip upon clinching a victory, injured himself needlessly, and been unable to play in the coming weeks? Skattebo had coach John Harbaugh previously convinced he had gained some wisdom after the coach read the player's quotes about his backflip last Friday. Harbaugh actually said in a press conference he was thinking of discussing the matter with Skattebo, but decided it wasn't necessary because the running back seemed to understand the celebration might not be in his or the team's best interest. But, nope. Skattebo in the air, feet above his head, relying on his feet and ankles to hold up during the landing and hoping his knees don't buckle. So, a conversation with Harbaugh is likely incoming. Skattebo is obviously valuable to the Giants. It's the reason they're not thrilled with these backflips in the first place. But while he's important to the team, he's also kind of just a solid player. If he weren't playing in New York, the chances of him being a marketing thing would be far smaller because, well, take Sunday as an example: THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! He rushed 14 times for 34 yards — a 2.4-yard-per-carry average. He caught three passes for 14 yards. And fumbled once, which he lost. So the guy is solid. And hard to figure out. And something of a frustration for Harbaugh. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Giants intercept Trevor Lawrence twice as they hold on to beat the Jaguars 23-18
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy threw a touchdown pass to Malik Nabers, Abdul Carter and the defense flustered Trevor Lawrence throughout and the New York Giants held on to defeat the Jacksonville Jaguars 23-18 on Sunday.
articles.body: J.J. McCarthy threw a touchdown pass to Malik Nabers, Abdul Carter and the defense flustered Trevor Lawrence throughout and the New York Giants held on to defeat the Jacksonville Jaguars 23-18 on Sunday, bouncing back from a bad loss and ending the AFC South leaders’ winning streak at three games. McCarthy made some important throws to balance out some inaccuracy and was a difference-maker with his legs. He scrambled for 33 yards and was 18 of 38 passing for 173 yards. Jameis Winston scored on a quarterback sneak, Dominic Zvada connected on 53- and 54-yard field goals and the Giants (6-3-1) survived Cam Skattebo fumbling for the fifth time this season. The offense that sputtered after going up by 14 points early in the fourth quarter got the job done late to seal the victory. Carter had two sacks to double his season total and end a four-game drought without one. His breakout performance came after pledging earlier in the week to show critics what he could do. New York did that as a team, 10 days after blowing a late lead against Washington that threatened to damage its chances of winning the NFC East. Beating Jacksonville allowed coach John Harbaugh’s team to maintain the same lead atop the division hours after Dallas crushed Tennessee 50-31. The Jaguars (7-3) lost for the first time in more than a month, with Lawrence throwing two interceptions and generally looking discombobulated. He was incomplete on a fourth-and-1 pass in the red zone and finished 25 of 47 for 301 yards. A lack of a consistent running game did not help Lawrence and the offense, which was without starting center Robert Hainsey, out because of a strained left knee and went 5 of 15 on third down. Jacksonville committed 13 penalties for 107 yards, continuing a troubling trend of undisciplined play. Coach Liam Coen challenged a crucial incomplete pass call on what he thought was a TD catch by Parker Washington in the back of the end zone early in the fourth quarter, and officials stuck with the initial ruling after video review.

articles.title: NFL says Parker Washington didn't control ball until he was out of bounds
articles.summary: Sunday's game between the Jaguars and Giants included a controversial decision in the fourth quarter on a play that looked like a touchdown catch by Jacksonv...
articles.body:
Sunday's game between the Jaguars and Giants included a controversial decision in the fourth quarter on a play that looked like a touchdown catch by Jacksonville receiver Parker Washington.

The ruling on the field was that the catch was incomplete. Jaguars coach Liam Coen challenged the decision.

Replay review confirmed the ruling on the field, even though CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore said during the broadcast that he believed it was a catch .

After the game, pool reporter Pat Leonard spoke with NFL V.P. of instant replay Mark Butterworth.

"The ruling on the field was an incomplete pass," Butterworth said. "First, to overturn a call, we need clear and obvious video evidence to overturn the on-field ruling. It was determined that the receiver did not gain full control of the ball until he was out of bounds."

Butterworth confirmed that he was referring to the fact that, when Washington hit the ground, the ball was moving in Washington's hands.

Still, movement of the ball is permitted. Washington objectively remained in control of the ball.

And here's the real point. Movement doesn't prevent clear and obvious evidence that the catch was made. The question should be this: Is it clear and obvious, given that movement is permitted, that Washington made the catch?

Most would say he did. If so, the ruling on the field should have been changed from incompletion to touchdown.

articles.title: 49ers’ Colton McKivitz suffers gruesome injury vs. Vikings
articles.summary: 49ers offensive lineman Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome injury on Sunday night.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have been dealt a devastating injury blow with right tackle Colton McKivitz in the first half of the Week 11 game against the Minnesota Vikings.

The injury occurred in the second quarter of the contest and it was immediately clear that the 49ers offensive lineman suffered a gruesome ankle injury.

McKivitz came down with the injury when he got his leg trapped under another player. You can check out video of the aftermath of the play in which McKivitz got hurt right here , but warning, it is hard to watch.

McKivitz stayed down on the field after the play and was tended to by the training staff before being loaded onto a cart and being taken off the field.

Players on both teams were obviously very distraught at the site of McKivitz's gruesome leg injury that is going to keep him out for the rest of the season.

The good news is, McKivitz was alert while leaving the field in the cart, but that doesn't change just how awful it was to see him get injured.

The loss is a tough one for the Niners, as McKivitz is one of the team's best offensive linemen, and he's one of the best right tackles in the sport.

Entering Week 11, McKivitz was having a phenomenal season with Pro Football Focus grades of 82.8 overall, 71.0 in pass-blocking and 88.8 in run-blocking, ranking seventh, 37th and second among tackles in the NFL.

McKivitz didn't allow a single sack and permitted just 12 pressures in 317 pass-blocking snaps.

Vederian Lowe is the next man up for San Francisco, but he will present a significant downgrade for the Niners' offense.

No team in the NFL has been as ravaged by injuries as San Francisco this season.

Going into the Sunday night game against the Vikings, the 49ers had a whopping 14 players on injured reserve . McKivitz will unfortunately be No. 15.

Despite all of their injuries, the Niners have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season.

Considering everything the Niners have had to overcome, there's no question head coach Kyle Shanahan is one of the top candidates for Coach of the Year.

articles.title: 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz carted off vs. Vikings with gruesome lower-leg injury

articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers right tackle Colton McKivitz left Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings with what looked like a significant injury to his lower left leg.

The injury took place during the second quarter of the game being played in Mexico City. McKivitz 's left leg got pinned under multiple players at the end a Christian McCaffrey run to his side.

When he pulled his leg from underneath the pile of players, his foot was twisted in the wrong direction.

Warning: Video below shows a graphic injury

McKivitz's teammates immediately knew that he'd sustained a significant injury. Multiple players took a knee around their injured teammate, and left tackle Trent Williams slammed his helmet into the turf, then held the back of his head in his hands.

Trainers rushed onto the field to tend to McKivitz. He was eventually taken off the field on a cart. McKivitz was upright and interacting with his teammates as they saw him off the field.

The nature of McKivitz's injury wasn't initially clear.

McKivitz is key to San Francisco's top-ranked offense. He's a strong run blocker who hasn't allowed a sack all season.

The 49ers have thrived despite injuries to key players on both sides of the ball throughout the season. They entered Sunday's game with the best record in the NFC at 8-1.
